title: Loss Functions — A Loss Shapes the Surface
key_insight: A smooth loss provides gradual slopes; a sharp or flat region can make steps unstable or uninformative. Surrogate losses replace a difficult real goal with a trainable approximation.
body:
## A Loss Shapes the Surface

Two objectives judge the same predictions differently, so they create different hills and valleys for the optimizer to travel.

A smooth loss provides gradual slopes; a sharp or flat region can make steps unstable or uninformative. Surrogate losses replace a difficult real goal with a trainable approximation.

For several goals, combine losses only after checking their scales. One large-numbered term can silently drown out every other objective.
common_mistakes: Loss is only a chart and never affects training.
The largest possible loss always means the best model.
One loss has the correct meaning for every output type.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “A Loss Shapes the Surface” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Training needs a meaningful numeric objective before it can decide how weights should change.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “A Loss Shapes the Surface” situation, explain Loss Functions without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
